title: Correctness and cost of a unary loop
statement: Let $c,C,q\in\mathbb{N}$ with $q>0$, let $x$ be a bit string, let $i<c+1$, and let $h:\{0,\ldots,c\}\to\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $h(k)=0$ whenever $k\le i$. Let $o$ be an output word, and let $r,j\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $j+r=q$. After exactly $r(\kappa_{q,C}(i)+2)+q+2$ steps of the unary box-enumeration machine from the configuration on input $x$ in state $\mathrm{loop}_i$, with tape contents $1^q$, output $o$, and head positions equal to $h$ except that head $i$ is at $j$, it reaches state $\mathrm{advance}_{i+1}$ with head positions $h$ and output $o$ followed by $rCq^i$ copies of $1$. Here $\kappa_{q,C}(0)=C+1$ and $\kappa_{q,C}(m+1)=q(\kappa_{q,C}(m)+2)+q+2$.
replaced: Let $c, C, q \in \mathbb{N}$ with $q > 0$, $x$ a bit string, $i \le c$, $h \colon \{0,\dots,c\} \to \mathbb{Z}$ with $h(k) = 0$ for every $k \le i$, $o$ an output word, and $r, j \in \mathbb{N}$ with $j + r = q$. Then running $\mathcal{P}_{c,C}$ for exactly $r\,(\kappa_{q,C}(i) + 2) + q + 2$ steps from $\Gamma_q(\mathrm{loop}_i, h[i \mapsto j], o)$ yields $\Gamma_q(\mathrm{advance}_{i+1}, h, o\,1^{rCq^i})$, where $\kappa_{q,C}(0) = C+1$ and $\kappa_{q,C}(r'+1) = q(\kappa_{q,C}(r')+2)+q+2$; here $\mathcal{P}_{c,C}$ is the unary box-enumeration machine with $c+1$ work tapes, which writes $1^{|x|+1}$ on every work tape and then runs $c+1$ nested unary loops, emitting $C$ ones per innermost iteration, and $\mathrm{loop}_i$, $\mathrm{rewind}_i$, $\mathrm{advance}_i$, $\mathrm{emit}_j$ are its control states, $\Gamma_q(s,h,o)$ denotes its configuration on input $x$ in control state $s$, with the input head on the blank cell right of the input, every work tape holding $1^q$ in cells $0,\dots,q-1$ and blanks elsewhere, work head $k$ at position $h(k)$, and output $o$, and $h[i \mapsto v]$ is $h$ with its $i$-th entry replaced by $v$.
